questions.title: How does the unified RoPE interpolation formula (Eq. 2) relate to the original RoPE angles?
questions.question_body: In the paper, Eq. 2 rewrites the RoPE embedding as a list of cos/sin terms with a factor `1/\lambda(\beta)^i`. I am confused about how this formulation is derived from the original RoPE definition in Eq. 1. Specifically, what does the term `\lambda(\beta)^i` represent mathematically, and how does changing `\lambda` correspond to scaling the rotation frequencies `\theta_i` used in standard RoPE? A concrete step‑by‑step derivation would help me understand how linear interpolation (PI), NTK‑based interpolation, and YaRN fit into this unified view.

questions.title: What is the intuition behind keeping the first \(\hat n\) tokens un‑interpolated?
questions.question_body: The authors claim that the initial tokens receive large attention scores and therefore should be exempt from positional interpolation (Finding 2). Why does reducing interpolation for these early positions improve perplexity? Is there empirical evidence that attention weights are indeed higher for the first few tokens, or is this mainly a heuristic? How does the choice of \(\hat n\) interact with different extension ratios (e.g., 8× vs 64×)?

questions.title: Why does imposing a monotonic non‑decreasing constraint on \(\lambda_i\) speed up the evolutionary search?
questions.question_body: The search algorithm enforces \(\lambda_i \le \lambda_{i+1}\) for all RoPE dimensions. The paper says this is motivated by NTK theory, but I don't see why such a constraint reduces the number of candidate solutions dramatically. Does it prune the search space exponentially, or just linearly? Also, could there be cases where the optimal solution violates monotonicity?

questions.title: How are the rescale factors \(\lambda_i\) applied during inference for different sequence lengths?
questions.question_body: During inference, LongRoPE dynamically adjusts RoPE rescale factors for short windows (4k, 8k) after fine‑tuning to 2048k. Is this done by swapping in a pre‑computed set of \(\lambda_i\) per target length, or by computing a scaling function on‑the‑fly? If the latter, what is the functional form? How does the model know which set of factors to use when the input length falls between two searched lengths?

questions.title: What exactly is being fine‑tuned in the progressive extension steps?
questions.question_body: The method first searches for RoPE factors for 128k, fine‑tunes 400 steps, then swaps to 256k factors and fine‑tunes another 600 steps. Are only the RoPE parameters updated during these steps, or are all model weights also trained? How does this limited fine‑tuning (1k steps total) avoid overfitting given the massive increase in context length?

questions.title: Why does a longer fine‑tuning window (256k) sometimes hurt performance compared to a shorter one (128k) as observed for Mistral?
questions.question_body: In Section 5.2 the authors note that Mistral fine‑tuned at 128k outperforms the 256k version on longer evaluations, attributing it to training on only 16k sequences during fine‑tuning. Could you clarify how training sequence length interacts with final context capability? Is there an optimal ratio between fine‑tuning length and target extension that balances stable training and extrapolation ability?

questions.title: How is perplexity computed for sequences longer than the model's native context window?
questions.question_body: The paper repeatedly reports perplexity at lengths up to 2048k even though LLaMA2/Mistral were originally trained with a 4k window. Do they use a sliding window approach, and if so, how are token probabilities merged across overlapping windows? Does this evaluation method faithfully reflect generation quality for truly contiguous million‑token inputs?

questions.title: Can you elaborate on the “information entropy” argument for non‑uniformity in RoPE dimensions?
questions.question_body: The authors claim that positional embedding exhibits "complex non-uniform information entropy" across dimensions and positions, which motivates dimension‑wise rescaling. What metric or experiment quantifies this entropy? Is there a theoretical justification (e.g., frequency coverage) that explains why lower frequency dimensions should be interpolated more aggressively?

questions.title: What are the limitations of LongRoPE when applied to architectures that do not use RoPE?
questions.question_body: LongRoPE is described as applicable to any LLM based on RoPE. For models using absolute sinusoidal embeddings or learned positional embeddings, could a similar evolutionary search be performed, or are there fundamental obstacles? How would one adapt the search space and constraints for non‑rotary positional schemes?

questions.title: How does LongRoPE interact with existing attention‑mask tricks for long context (e.g., Sliding‑Window or Global‑Local attention)?
questions.question_body: The related work mentions attention‑based extensions as complementary to positional interpolation. If we combine LongRoPE's rescaled RoPE with a sparse attention pattern designed for million‑token inputs, would there be any interference (e.g., double counting of position information)? Has any experiment been reported that stacks both techniques?
